## Known gaps

- **Admin commands need the Blob store opener (request 3).** On this branch `hangar admin backup`, `restore` and `doctor` stop at the Blob store step unless `--skip-blobs` is given; they are tested with `blobtest.Fake`.
- **The smoke test beyond `/healthz` has not run against a real server**, because this branch's binary serves phase 0 stand-ins (login answers 501). The CLI's client side is tested against the fake Instance only; the integration lead should run `scripts/smoke.sh` and `go test -tags compat ./compat/lmstudio` with `HANGAR_LMSTUDIO_URL` against the wired binary.
- **LM Studio's `downloadsFolder` key** is read as documented in its settings file but not verified against an LM Studio install (none on the build machine). The home-folder lookup follows LM Studio's own `findLMStudioHome` code. The manual check is in `compat/lmstudio/README.md`.
- **S3 providers other than MinIO** are documented, not tested (W1 has the same gap for AWS).
- **The release, docs and compat workflows have only been linted**, and their action refs resolved (`scripts/check-action-refs.sh`); they first run on GitHub. Trivy and the Homebrew tap were not exercised locally, and cosign keyless signing needs GitHub's OIDC token. The chart job's registry login was reproduced against a local registry with password authentication: cosign 3.1.3 cannot sign with only Helm's login and can with a Docker-config login, which the job now has. GoReleaser ran as a snapshot without signing or SBOMs.
- **k6 scripts** were syntax-checked, not run against an Instance; `docs/benchmarks.md` is phase 3's.
- **The Grafana dashboard's PromQL** was loaded but not executed against Prometheus; names follow the exporter's rules and `TestReferences` checks the mapping.
- **The Kibana dashboard expects cumulative metric temporality**; the Job and Blob store latency percentiles come from cumulative histograms (documented).
- **Docs name UI labels** (for example **Settings**, **Upstream tokens**) from 09-web-ui.md; phase 3's walk-through should check them against W8's UI.
- **The image has no shell.** If any server code runs `sh` (git hooks, for example), it fails in the container; W3's git server runs only the git binary as far as its handoff says.
- **DuckDB's `hf://`** is documented as huggingface.co-only; W10 checks whether it honours a custom endpoint.

## Corrections (2026-10-14)

An independent check found these in the first handoff. Each is fixed on the branch.

- **A 45 MB macOS build of `hangar` was committed at the repository root** in the first CLI commit, and the handoff did not say so. The branch history was rewritten to drop it (every W9 commit has a new SHA; no other branch pointed at them). `.gitignore` now ignores `/hangar` and `/hangar.exe`, and `.dockerignore` keeps them out of the image build context.
- **`make lint-deploy` failed**, although the handoff said it and `shellcheck` passed: shellcheck 0.11.0 reported SC2013 (info) in `scripts/fuzz.sh`, which exits 1. The script now reads targets line by line on their own file descriptors; `shellcheck scripts/*.sh loadtest/*.sh` and `make lint-deploy` exit 0, and `scripts/fuzz.sh 3s` still runs the one fuzz target.
- **Presigned URLs could reach CLI output.** `push` wrapped the HTTP client error for a part upload, and every request through `client.do` wrapped its error, so a failed presigned part upload or a failed redirect to a presigned download printed the URL with its signature. All requests now go through `redactingDoer` (see 08 CLI above). Tests: `TestPushDoesNotPrintPresignedPartURLs` and `TestPullDoesNotPrintPresignedDownloadURLs` fail without the fix; the fake Instance gained `RedirectDownloads` and serves presigned URLs on another origin.
- **`--json` was not on every command**: `hangar logout` had none. It has now, and a test checks every command.
- **The missing Home page demo was not listed** as a gap. It is now, with the script that records it.


## Corrections, second check (2026-10-14)

A second independent check found these. Each is fixed on the branch; the demo and screenshot are integration items (see What the integration lead must wire).

- **Two GitHub Action refs did not exist**, so the workflows using them would fail at "Set up job": `astral-sh/setup-uv@v10` (only `v10.0.0` to `v10.3.0` exist) in `ci.yml`, `compat.yml`, `docs.yml` and `release.yml`, and `sigstore/cosign-installer@v4` (only `v4.0.0` to `v4.1.2`) three times in `release.yml`. They are now `@v10.3.0` and `@v4.1.2`. `scripts/check-action-refs.sh`, run by `make lint-deploy` and so by CI, resolves every `uses:` ref with `git ls-remote` and fails on one that does not exist: on the old workflows it reports exactly these two, and on the new ones `All 26 action refs exist.`
- **`TestPushResumesAfterAFailedPart` was flaky.** The four parts go up in parallel, so when the injected failure of part 3 came first the push stopped before any other part was stored and `PartPuts() >= 1` failed. The fake Instance gained `FailPartLast`, which answers the failure only once the upload's other parts are stored (or the request ends, or `PartFailureWait` passes), with its own test. The push test now asserts exactly 3 parts stored after the failure and exactly 1 sent on resume. `go test -race -count=100 -cpu 1,2,4 -run TestPushResumesAfterAFailedPart ./internal/cli/` (300 runs) and `go test -race -count=8 -cpu 1,4 ./internal/cli/...` pass.
- **The release chart job could not have signed the chart.** `helm registry login` writes Helm's own registry config, which cosign does not read, so `cosign sign` on the chart would have been refused by GHCR. The job now also runs `docker/login-action`, uses `shell: bash` (so a failed `helm push` fails the step instead of being hidden by `tee`), and stops if `helm push` printed no 64-digit digest.
- **`--json` was not on every command**: `hangar version`, `healthcheck`, `config reference`, `config validate` and `admin migrate` had none (request 12).
- **The first release-please pull request.** The check expected 0.1.0. release-please 17.6.0 (what `release-please-action@v5` locks) reads a manifest version of `0.0.0` as "never released" and proposes 1.0.0, but only by default; `release-please-config.json` now sets `initial-version: "1.0.0"`, and `CONTRIBUTING.md` explains it and the `Release-As:` footer.
- **The image did not read `/etc/hangar/hangar.yaml`** unless `HANGAR_CONFIG` was set. It now sets it and ships a file there that sets nothing; the Docker docs no longer ask for the variable.
- **The image row quoted a version from before the history rewrite.** It now quotes the rebuilt image.

## Security fixes and follow-ups, third check (2026-10-14)

A third check and a background commit review found these. Each is fixed on the branch with a test that fails on the files from before the fix (checked by running the new tests in a worktree at `2a1a631`: 5 tests fail there, 32 findings).

- **Security: the Compose examples shipped default credentials and exposed MinIO.** `postgres-minio.yaml` and `scale.yaml` fell back to `hangar-example-password` for Postgres and `hangar-example-secret` for the MinIO root user, and `postgres-minio.yaml` published the MinIO console on `0.0.0.0:9001`, so anyone on the network could sign in to MinIO and read or overwrite every Blob, bypassing Hangar's authorisation. `oidc-keycloak.yaml` set `KC_BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD: admin` and published Keycloak on `0.0.0.0:8081`, and the realm and Hangar's provider JSON carried a fixed client secret. Now:
  - every secret is `${VAR:?message}` with no fallback (`POSTGRES_PASSWORD`, `MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD`, `HANGAR_INSTANCE_KEY`, `HANGAR_ADMIN_PASSWORD` in `scale.yaml`, `KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_PASSWORD`, `HANGAR_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET`); the one exception is `${HANGAR_ADMIN_PASSWORD:-}` in the single-replica examples, where empty makes Hangar generate a password and print it once;
  - the realm reads the client secret through Keycloak's `${HANGAR_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET}` placeholder;
  - the MinIO console (`127.0.0.1:9001`), the unauthenticated Traefik dashboard (`127.0.0.1:8082`) and Keycloak (`127.0.0.1:8081`) are published on loopback only; Postgres and the MinIO API stay unpublished. Hangar now reaches Keycloak through the network alias `keycloak.localhost` instead of `host-gateway`, which needed the port on every interface;
  - `docs/get-started/compose.md` (new "Create the secrets" section) and the file headers give one command that writes all six values into `deploy/compose/.env` with `openssl rand`, mode 0600, refusing to overwrite an existing file (`set -C`); `.gitignore` ignores `.env`;
  - `scripts/compose-smoke.sh` generates fresh values for every variable, and `make lint-deploy` passes dummies to `docker compose config`.

  Tests (`deploy/deploy_test.go`, run by `make test`): `TestComposeSecretsHaveNoDefaults`, `TestComposeOnlyHangarListensOnEveryInterface`, `TestKeycloakRealmClientSecretComesFromTheEnvironment`, plus `TestComposeSecretChecksCatchDefaults` and `TestComposePortCheckCatchesExposedPorts`, which pin the checks to the forms they must catch. Checked live: `docker compose config` with no environment stops and names each missing variable; with the Keycloak example up, the client secret from the environment authenticates (`unauthorized_client: Client not enabled to retrieve service account`) and the old one is refused (`Invalid client credentials`), `admin`/`admin` gets 401 and `KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_PASSWORD` 200, Keycloak listens on `127.0.0.1:8081` only, and the Hangar image resolves `keycloak.localhost` on the Compose network and gets Keycloak's answer, whose discovery document has the issuer `http://keycloak.localhost:8081/realms/hangar`. A `.env` written by the documented command is read by Compose unchanged.
- **Helm, the same class of problem.** The chart itself has no default credentials (it generates the Instance key and admin password, `randAscii 32` and `randAlphaNum 24`, into a Secret) and exposes nothing beyond a ClusterIP Service unless asked. `deploy/helm/examples/scale-values.yaml`, which the Helm guide links as the fuller example, put a Postgres DSN with password `hangar` and an S3 secret key in `secrets:`. It now uses `existingSecret: hangar-secrets` and shows the `kubectl create secret` command with `openssl rand` values. Test: `TestHelmExampleValuesHoldNoCredentials` (example and `ci/` values must have no `secrets:`). So that lint still renders the chart's own Secrets, `make lint-deploy` renders the scale values once more with a dummy `secrets.HANGAR_DATABASE_DSN` (kubeconform 19/19 valid). Considered and left: with `networkPolicy.enabled` and metrics on, the metrics port accepts any source; it serves no credentials, and narrowing it is a values change for operators.
- **The README Helm command failed**: `helm install hangar oci://ghcr.io/jamesagarside/charts/hangar` stops on the chart's required `publicURL`. It now sets `--set publicURL=https://hangar.example.com`, says what the value is, and links the Helm guide. Test: `TestHelmInstallCommandsSetPublicURL` checks every `helm install` and `helm upgrade` of the chart in `README.md` and `docs/` (outside `spec` and `build`) for `publicURL` or a values file, with `TestSetsPublicURL` for the parser.
- **The Docker backup command in `docs/operate/backup.md` could not work on Linux**: it bind-mounted the host's `/backups`, which belongs to root, into a container running as UID 65532 (`--user` is no way out, because Hangar then cannot read its own data volume). The image now has a `/backups` folder owned by 65532 (mode 0700), so a new named volume mounted there takes that owner. The page has a "Back up a container" section: back up into the `hangar-backups` volume, copy out with `docker create` and `docker cp`, restore from the volume with `--force`, or, on Linux, give a host folder to 65532 with `sudo install -d -o 65532 -g 65532 -m 0700`. Test: `scripts/image-backup-check.sh <image>`, run by `ci.yml` after the configuration check, which migrates a volume, backs up into a new named volume at `/backups`, copies the backup out with `docker cp` and restores it. Against the image built from `2a1a631` it fails with `Error: mkdir /backups/check: permission denied`; against this branch it passes. The host-folder recipe was checked with a root-owned volume (fails the same way) that was then given to 65532 (backup succeeds). The check uses `--skip-blobs`, because this branch's binary has no Blob store opener (Known gaps); the permission failure happens before any object is read.

## Bellatrix preview fixes (fix/pf1-upload, 2026-10-17)

- **Part and download retries** (finding 8). `sendPart` and `downloader.get` retry a transfer that may succeed again (a transport error, 408, 425, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504) up to `transferAttempts` (6) times with exponential backoff and jitter (1 to 30 seconds) or Retry-After. A presigned part URL that answers 403 is renewed once by planning the file again. Progress counts a resent part or resumed download once (`countingProgress`). Tests: `TestPushRetriesFailedParts` (503, 500, connection reset half way through the body), `TestPushDoesNotRetryAPartTheInstanceRefuses`, `TestPushRenewsExpiredPartURLs`, `TestPullRetriesABrokenDownload`, with new `clitest` faults `FailPartStatus`, `ResetPart`, `StalePartURLs`, `DropCompletion` and `FailDownload`.
- **Completion cut off by a proxy** (finding 13c). `complete` resends after a transport error, 502, 504, 408 or 429, and on a 404 after a resend plans the file again; `exists` means an earlier completion finished it. The 503 with Retry-After handling was already done in `071ee7d`. Test: `TestPushFinishesACompletionAProxyCutOff`.
- **Import status lines** (finding 10). `hangar import` prints "Looking up <repo> on <upstream>", "Creating a Mirror of <repo>", a hashing progress for files whose SHA-256 is unknown, "Uploading N files, X to <repo>." and "Checking <file> (<size>) on the Instance"; on a terminal a waiting line counts the seconds (`waitStatus`). Tests: `TestImportSaysWhatItIsWaitingFor`, `TestWaitStatusOnATerminal`.
- `GET /me` answers 204 when nobody is signed in (finding 6); `client.me` reports that as not signed in.
- The compat harness's temporary binary leak was already fixed in `1e0b1cb` (`harness.Main`, and an `atexit` hook in `compat/hangar_instance.py`). `compat/hf` now calls `harness.Main` from `TestMain` for its MinIO test.

## Fixes from the bellatrix preview (2026-10-17, branch `fix/pf1-chart`)

James ran the preview on his home cluster under Argo CD, with Postgres in the same Application and MinIO behind Nginx Proxy Manager. Findings 2 to 5 and 13d of that run are fixed here, each with a test that fails on the chart and docs at `c79363e`.

- **Migrations without Helm hooks (finding 2).** Argo CD runs Helm's pre-install and pre-upgrade hooks as `PreSync` hooks before anything else, so with Postgres in the same Application the migrate Job waited for a database that was never created. New value `migrations.mode`: `hook` (default, unchanged) or `initContainer`, which renders no hooks other than the `helm test` Pod and gives every `web` and `worker` Pod a `migrate` init container with the same env and envFrom as Hangar. It fails and is retried until Postgres answers; `bun` migration locking keeps Pods that start together from migrating twice. Unknown modes fail the render. Tests: `TestChartMigrationModes` (offline) and `TestKindGitOpsInstall`, which renders `deploy/helm/examples/gitops-values.yaml` with no cluster access, as Argo CD does, applies it together with Postgres and MinIO in one `kubectl apply`, and waits for `web` and `worker` to be ready.
- **Generated secrets under helm template and Argo CD (finding 3).** `lookup` returns nothing there, so every render made a new Instance key. The chart now checks that `lookup` reaches the cluster (the release namespace's `default` ServiceAccount, or the `default` namespace for a first install with `--create-namespace`) and otherwise stops with an error that names `existingSecret` and links the new guide section. Consequence: `helm lint`, `ct lint` and offline renders of `ci/default-values.yaml` now pass `--set generateSecrets=false` (`Makefile` `lint-deploy`, `compat.yml`); generation is covered on a cluster. Tests: `TestChartGenerateSecretsNeedsCluster` (offline), `TestKindGeneratedSecretsSurviveRenders` (install, `helm template --dry-run=server` and `helm upgrade` keep the key) and `TestKindNotesReadOnlyRenderedSecretKeys` (the two NOTES cases that generate secrets moved here from `TestChartNotesReadOnlyRenderedSecretKeys`, which keeps the four offline cases).
- **Secret checksum and cache volume (finding 4).** `checksum/secret` now hashes `secrets`, the `existingSecret` name and, when `lookup` works, the existing Secret's data, so renaming the Secret (GitOps) or changing its data (`helm upgrade`) restarts the Pods. `cacheSizeLimit` defaults to 16Gi (was 10Gi, equal to `git.cache_size`), and the chart refuses values where the cache volume is less than 1.25 times `git.cache_size` while the cache is on that volume. Tests: `TestChartSecretChecksumFollowsExistingSecret`, `TestChartCacheVolumeOutgrowsGitCache`.
- **MinIO region (finding 5).** `docs/operate/storage.md` says to use the region MinIO is configured with; the Compose files say why they use `us-east-1`. Test: `TestStorageDocsMinIORegion`.
- **nginx in front of MinIO or Hangar (finding 13d).** `docs/operate/proxies.md` has a "Large files through nginx" section (each directive and why, the 1 GiB `proxy_max_temp_file_size` failure, MinIO server block, Nginx Proxy Manager, ingress-nginx annotations). Test: `TestProxyDocsNginxStreamsLargeFiles` (every nginx example sets the directives; there are Hangar and MinIO examples).
- **Guide.** `docs/get-started/helm.md` has "Run with Argo CD": why hooks and `lookup` differ, the Secret, an `Application` with `valuesObject`, rotation and the persistence alternative.

Run: `make lint-deploy` (offline), `make test-kind IMAGE=<local image>` (`scripts/kind-chart-test.sh`: throwaway kind cluster with its own kubeconfig, deleted afterwards). CI runs the cluster tests in the "Helm chart on kind" job after `ct install`.

## Bellatrix preview fixes, round 2 (fix/pf2-upload, 2026-10-17)

- **Other files carry on** (finding 8, second half). `uploader.upload` no longer returns on the first file that fails after its retries: it uploads the rest and returns the operations for the files on the Instance with an `*uploadFailures` that names each failed file (and unwraps to their errors, so exit codes still come from the API error). `commitFiles` makes no Commit then, so the next run sends only the failed files' missing parts. `importAsMirror` pulls the files that went up into the Mirror and reports the failure on that Repo's result; `importSnapshot` never falls back to a local Repo because of an upload failure. A cancelled context still stops at once. Tests: `TestPushCarriesOnAfterAFileFails`, `TestPushNamesEveryFileThatFailed`, `TestImportCarriesOnAfterAFileFails`.
